newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo drops amid downgrade, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo drops amid downgrade, profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped on Wednesday as analysts at Goldman Sachs trimmed earnings estimates the day before the drug giant's results and the sector retreated from recent gains, dealers said.

Separately, reports in a U.S. medical journal found side-effects from extended use of inhaled steroids of an increased risk of glaucoma in elderly people, analysts said, but they played down the significance for Glaxo of the Canadian findings.
"I don't think anyone will exactly be rushing to downgrade figures as a result of this study," said one. "The sector had a good run earlier this week and they are all off a bit today."
Glaxo is a major manufacturer of asthma inhalers. The stock, which hit a high of 10.63 stg earlier in the session, was down 26-1/2p at 10.29-1/2 stg by 1115 GMT in volume of 4.7 million shares.
No-one from the company was immediately available for comment.
Reflecting the continued strength of sterling, Goldman cut its earnings estimate for Glaxo to 56.8p per shares from 57.4p for 1996 and its 1997 estimate to 55.1p from 58.0p.
It also trimmed estimates on other drug stocks, with SmithKline Beecham Plc cut to 40.6p from 41.7p for 1997 and 46.9p from 48.2p for 1998. SmithKline shares were down 12p at 909.
Zeneca Group Plc was cut to 74.3p from 79.3p for 1997 and to 85.9p from 91.9p for 1998. The stock was down 28-1/2p at 18.54 stg.
